text:
eli: Quick check — should we prefer FlashAttention v3 on H100s in eu-west for the new gptx-l rollout? I ran short benches vs Triton vendor kernels and got mixed signals. chart: https://imgur.com/a/bench-eu-west

sophia: saw the chart. flashv3 wins on median latency for seq<=1024 and batches 1–8, ~10-15% p50 improvement vs triton. but p99 regresses around seq=2048+ when kv-cache grows.

mike: can you paste the throughput curves or a tiny table? numbers make it easier to reason about capacity sizing.

bench-bot: summary from last run (eu-west, L40 H100, model=gptx-l, q8f16 / q4f16 both tested):
```
config, p50(ms), p95(ms), p99(ms), tokens/s
flashv3 q8f16 b=1 s=512, 14.2, 58, 112, 950
triton q8f16 b=1 s=512, 16.0, 60, 98, 880
flashv3 q8f16 b=8 s=512, 47, 210, 420, 6800
triton q8f16 b=8 s=512, 55, 195, 380, 7200
flashv3 q8f16 b=16 s=2048, 320, 1100, 2100, 15000
triton q8f16 b=16 s=2048, 360, 900, 1600, 17000
```

eli: interesting — flashv3 gives better median but p99 spikes for long context + larger batches. that matches my local reproducer.

devon: we also saw a small quality jitter in q8f16 with flashv3 for some completion endpoints (narrow beam on names/ids). not huge but shows up in the eval set (delta in token accuracy ~0.8%).

sophia: that matters if we care about strict quality SLOs. proposal: use a decision matrix by workload profile (latency-sensitive vs throughput-sensitive vs quality-sensitive) + region.

mike: Agreed. Example rules: prefer flashv3 for low-batch, short-seq, latency-critical routes; prefer triton/vendor lib for heavy throughput batches and long-context to avoid p99 and throughput regressions; pin q4 for experiments where quality is critical.

eli: here's a draft routing snippet we could add to the router policy (pseudo-yaml):
```
routes:
  - name: low-latency
    conditions:
      - seq_len <= 1024
      - batch_size <= 8
    prefer: flashv3
  - name: long-context-throughput
    conditions:
      - seq_len > 1024
      - batch_size >= 8
    prefer: triton_vendor
  - name: quality-sensitive
    conditions:
      - route_tag == "high-quality"
    prefer: triton_vendor
fallback: triton_vendor
p99_threshold_ms: 120
```

mike: can we add an auto-hysteresis that switches to fallback if observed p99 > p99_threshold for 15m? avoid flapping.

sophia: yes — implement windowed metric check and require sustained breach + cooldown. also provide telemetry: per-route token-rate, p50/p95/p99, and a small sample of failing requests for qa.

devon: for the q8 experiments, let's gate by eval-run pass rate. if quality regression > 0.5% on a predefined eval set, auto-block the route flip.

eli: plan: run a 12h mixed workload campaign in eu-west (traffic replay 0.5x) with flashv3 canary at 10%. collect p50/p95/p99 + eval regression signals. if all good, bump to 30% for 48h then decide.

mike: sounds good. assign tasks? eli -> run nightly campaign and post detailed CSVs. sophia -> hook up the p99 auto-hysteresis and dashboards. devon -> add the eval gating check. bench-bot -> run nightly overnight job and post aggregated metrics to this thread. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: scheduled bench job id=eu-west-flashv3-canary-2026-03-21-00Z, will post results here when done.

eli: thanks — tagging @mike @sophia @devon. will start the run in ~10 min.
